The body of evidence suggests that the notion that new myofiber formation contributes to loading-induced muscle hypertrophy in humans is questionable. If a contribution does exist, its impact on increases in muscle cross-sectional area appears to be minimal (6). Most likely, humans cannot naturally increase muscle size to reach the critical threshold that warrants fiber splitting. It remains possible that administration of supraphysiological doses of illicit anabolic agents may result in extreme hypertrophy that allows individuals to exceed the limits of hypertrophic capacity
